title: POC weekly: Dedicated reserve & burst planning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on dedicated sizing for bursts, autoscaling thresholds, KV/prefix cache hit rate impact, and an ops playbook for fallback. Agreed to run a simulated 10x burst next Tuesday and to share a revised sizing worksheet + pricing for a reserved baseline with 30% burst headroom.
next_steps: Redwood: Share revised dedicated sizing worksheet and pricing by 2025-12-05
Customer: Provide 72-hour traffic trace and sample prompts by 2025-12-04
Joint: Run 10x burst simulation on 2025-12-09 (engineer runbook)
action_items: Alex Chen | Send dedicated sizing worksheet + pricing sheet | due 2025-12-05
Priya Nair | Prepare burst simulation playbook and failure-mode checklist | due 2025-12-08
Jordan Blake | Upload 72hr traffic dump + top 10 prompt templates to shared S3 | due 2025-12-04
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: ok everyone thanks for joining, this is the weekly POC sync for Cobalt, we are at 9:30 PT. quick roll call?
[00:07] Maria Torres: Maria here, yeah, morning.
[00:10] Jordan Blake: Jordan on eng. Samir's dialed in but might join late.
[00:15] Samir Patel: hey team, here—sorry, slightly delayed.
[00:23] Alex Chen: great. Priya from Redwood?
[00:25] Priya Nair: hi all, Priya Nair, SE on the account. I'll take the deep infra notes.
[00:32] Alex Chen: cool. quick agenda: review last week's throughput run, look at latency and 95th percentile during the burst window, talk autoscale thresholds and reserved baseline, then agree next steps.
[00:45] Maria Torres: sounds good. we saw production-like tests last week that spiked at about 8x baseline for roughly 12 minutes.
[00:52] Jordan Blake: yeah to add, CPU and GPU metrics looked fine but we saw token generation time jump and some KV cache misses, which I think increased latency.
[01:05] Priya Nair: right, we pulled the logs — KV (K V) cache hit rate dropped from our expected 87% to about 54% during the peak. that changed the dynamic because you lose prefix reuse and your effective per-token compute jumps.
[01:22] Alex Chen: and that interacts with batching too, correct? lower cache hit means more per-request compute so the same batch size increases tail latency.
[01:31] Priya Nair: exactly. the continuous batching assumes a high prefix reuse; when cache misses spike, you get more memory movement and kernel stalls. we instrumented a run with smaller batch targets and saw 95th drop by ~200ms but cost went up ~11%.
[01:47] Jordan Blake: Maria — were those prompts mostly longer sequences? I remember the test had a lot of multi-turn medical summaries, so tokens per request were higher.
[01:55] Maria Torres: yes, average sequence length was ~420 tokens, top 10 prompts often hit 1k tokens once you include conversation history.
[02:04] Priya Nair: that's important for sizing. longer sequences reduce batch packing efficiency and extend kernel runtime which increases contention. for dedicated pools, we recommend planning for worst-case sequence percentiles, not just median.
[02:19] Alex Chen: ok so on to autoscale policy. we proposed min_replicas 2, target_latency_ms 250, scale_step 1, cool_down 90s in the doc. any pushback?
[02:33] Samir Patel: Samir here — we worry min_replicas=2 might be small for our SLAs during long bursts, because spin-up for new replicas measured at ~70s in our last run. if we have a 30s user timeout, that's bad.
[02:47] Priya Nair: good point — startup time includes model load, KV warm-up. we can do a warm-standby pool (reserved baseline) to keep more reps hot; that's what reserved_capacity is for.
[02:57] Alex Chen: the tradeoff is cost. keeping more GPUs reserved inflates steady-state. we proposed a hybrid: reserve baseline for 60% of expected sustained traffic and autoscale on top for spikes.
[03:11] Jordan Blake: can you quantify? what would 60% baseline for our numbers mean?
[03:16] Priya Nair: based on your 72-hour trace, median concurrent tokens mapped to about 12 effective vworkers on A100-80GB equiv. 60% baseline -> 7 dedicated workers reserved, with autoscale allowed up to 18 for extreme peaks.
[03:30] Maria Torres: that's a big jump; what's the cost delta between reserved 7 vs 2?
[03:35] Alex Chen: ballpark monthly reserved cost for 7 on our Dedicated SKU is in the pricing sheet we shared — I'll reshare, but it's about 3.6x the cost of the 2-reserve scenario. however on a per-token basis during bursts the cost is lower because autoscale avoid expensive on-demand cold starts.
[03:52] Samir Patel: curious about fallback policies — we saw in previous calls mention of automatic model fallback to smaller quantized variants. does Redwood do that?
[04:01] Priya Nair: yes we have a policy routing layer: you can define fallback to a bfloat16 quantized variant or a smaller param model (e.g., 13B -> 6B-ish) when latency or queue depth crosses thresholds. but there is a quality delta that QA must accept. we can tie fallback to percent of request types or to user segments.
[04:20] Maria Torres: quality delta is sensitive — in clinical summarization we can't drop model quality for accuracy reasons. so fallback is risky for certain paths.
[04:28] Jordan Blake: for non-critical background tasks (e.g., suggestions, auto-tagging) fallback ok. for patient-facing summarization we need stronger guarantees.
[04:38] Alex Chen: good segmentation approach. you can route high-sensitivity workflows always to reserved baseline, and lower-sensitivity to autoscale/fallback policies.
[04:49] Priya Nair: another lever is KV cache sizing and priming. if you pre-warm KV for top 200 prompts we saw hit rate go back to ~81%, which dropped tail by about 140ms in our microbench. it's cheap compared to 1-2 GPUs.
[05:02] Samir Patel: that might be the most cost-effective first step. Jordan, can you prioritize top prompts?
[05:07] Jordan Blake: yes we'll extract top 200 by Friday.
[05:10] Maria Torres: security question — Samir flagged SOC2 compliance and audit logs for production. do we have those artifacts?
[05:17] Alex Chen: yes, Redwood has SOC2 Type II and can provide whitepaper + attestations. I'll attach the security pack. also we support KMS integrations for key management in Private deployments; for Dedicated we can do customer managed keys via our VPC flows.
[05:33] Samir Patel: nice. also need to confirm data residency — some customers require EU region storage.
[05:38] Priya Nair: we can pin region; for POC if you want us to run the burst sim in eu-west we can — might change instance types slightly.
[05:47] Jordan Blake: let's keep the sim in us-west first, then replicate in eu if needed.
[05:52] Alex Chen: back to autoscale: Priya suggested adjusting cool_down to 120s and having a rapid scale_up step of 2 replicas to respond faster without overprovisioning. thoughts?
[06:04] Priya Nair: yes scale_step=2 helps for abrupt 3-10x bursts if you also have a slightly higher target_latency_ms e.g., 300ms so you avoid thrash. combined with reserved baseline it smooths the user impact.
[06:16] Samir Patel: will that still meet our 95th SLO of 350ms?
[06:20] Priya Nair: based on our sim tuning, with 7 reserved and scale_step=2, 95th stays under 320ms in the 10x burst test if KV hit rates above 70%. if KV drops to 50% you'll be closer to 420ms.
[06:35] Jordan Blake: then improving cache hit is critical. what about prefix caching TTLs? we had short TTLs in our POC config.
[06:42] Priya Nair: increasing TTLs for your top prompt families helps; also consider a small warm-up step where we precompute and store top prefixes in the cache store on surge detection. that's part of the burst playbook we'll share.
[06:56] Alex Chen: on monitoring and alerts, we propose token-level dashboards, 95/99 latency traces, and an alert when cache hit rate < 65% or queue depth > 12. any additions?
[07:08] Maria Torres: can we add an alert for model loading errors and a runbook link? we hit a model load OOM once last week.
[07:15] Priya Nair: yes we'll add model_load_error alert and link to failure-mode checklist. we'll also include an automated rollback to a previous stable model variant if load fails more than twice in five minutes.
[07:29] Samir Patel: what about the billing implications of reserving warm pool vs on-demand? we want a hybrid table to show marginal cost per extra percent of availability.
[07:39] Alex Chen: agreed — action item for me to send a marginal cost table and a couple scenarios (2-reserve vs 7-reserve vs 10-reserve).
[07:47] Jordan Blake: regarding the simulation on 2025-12-09, what's the exact run plan?
[07:52] Priya Nair: plan: 1) baseline 20 minutes at median qps, 2) ramp up 10x over 2 minutes, sustain 12 minutes, then ramp down; we'll run three iterations with different cache priming strategies: no warm, pre-warm top-50, pre-warm top-200. ops will capture latency, cost, and model quality samples.
[08:12] Maria Torres: perfect. can you add a canary step where we route 5% of live traffic to the new autoscale policy to validate in prod?
[08:20] Alex Chen: yes that's doable — can do a canary after successful sim.
[08:24] Samir Patel: last question — any known perf differences between A100 and L4 for our model? we test on A100 but wondered if cheaper L4 could be viable.
[08:32] Priya Nair: L4 is ok for smaller sequence lengths and quantized models; for 1k token runs A100s win on memory headroom and tail latency. we can benchmark a mixed fleet but expect 15-25% higher latency on L4 for long sequences.
[08:48] Alex Chen: ok let's capture that as a risk in the doc.
[08:52] Maria Torres: thanks everyone, this was useful. recap and next steps?
[08:58] Alex Chen: recap: Redwood to share updated sizing worksheet + pricing, marginal cost scenarios, security pack; Priya to share burst playbook and alerts/runbooks; Customer to provide 72hr trace and top prompts. Run scheduled sim 2025-12-09.
[09:10] Jordan Blake: I'll upload the traces by Friday.
[09:13] Samir Patel: we'll review security pack and get back with any legal questions.
[09:18] Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the 12/09 run and attach docs.
[09:24] (call ends) 

Notes: artifacts mentioned — dedicated-sizing-sheet (internal link), /s3/cobalt/traffic/72hr_dump.zip, security-pack-soc2.pdf. There was a short period of crosstalk at 06:00-06:04, and a transcription hiccup where "K-V" was transcribed as "K V" in some segments.
